page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top, with "Cap.17." at the left and "AVGVSTINVS" at the right. Continuation of a paragraph from the previous page at the top. Below it a headpiece ornament, then the chapter heading "CAP. XVII." with its subtitle. Then the italic paragraph with a large decorative initial. At the foot, a note in full-measure text, marked by "I" and "{1}" in the text. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Rex,Spiritus,Sciens,discooperiens,præcipiens, Iesus Nazarenus: quæ quanquam nihil nisi verum de Christo enuntient, quia tamen sine fide & verbo Dei fiunt, merito & magicæ incantationes à patribus appellantur: & non preces, sed ut peccata grauissima esse censentur, & damnari debent.
main_text.head: CAP. XVII.
Ophitæ unde dicti, & eorum erroris caput duplex hic comprehensum.

p.i: Ophita à colubro nominati{1} sunt. Coluber enim Græce ὄφις dicitur. Hunc autem colubrum, qui decepit Adam & Euam Christum arbitrantur. Sed habent etiam verum colubrum, quem nutriunt, & venerantur, qui & incantante sacerdote egreditur de spelunca, & ascendit super altare innixum spelunca, & oblationes eorum lambit, & inuoluens se circa eas regreditur ad speluncam, & ita confringunt oblationes in Eucharistiam, quasi à serpente Christo sanctificatas. Tradunt huius serpentis cultum à Nicolaitis siue Gnosticis ad ipsos deductum.

main_text.p: I Nominati.) Varijs nominibus ab eodem fonte deductis hi nominantur, nimirum Ophitæ, Ophei, & Ophiomorphi, vti à Theodoreto lib.1. ne nos nominum diuersitas fallat, & diuersos esse existimemus, qui sunt ijdem. Hos cum Sethianis quidam coniungunt: alij cum Nicolaitis

page.notes: The decorative initial is an O, joined to "phita" as "Ophita". The printed word appears as "Phita" with the O in the woodcut; the first letter is taken from the ornament. The superscript "1" in the text and the "I" before the note refer to the same mark; the note's marker is printed as "I". "Christo" and "Euam" are as printed. The headpiece ornament and the rule above "CAP. XVII." are decoration and not transcribed. The note at the foot is printed at full measure with no separate small type.
